answers.question: What is your biggest lesson from observing Malaysian property investors so far?
answers.answer: Each area has distinct market characteristics and culture, thus affecting investor preference and purchase decision. Value appreciation is stagnant but rental demand is still healthy, so investors are mainly focusing on holding the property long term and ensure healthy monthly cash flow from rental properties. However, most of them are looking at just the numbers without considering other aspects of the property. I have a theory. When they are just focusing on data, when market turns bad, every property becomes undervalued and cheap. Then how they can decide which one is temporarily cheap (will eventually increase in value back to norm), while some properties will only became cheaper and the market value will drop indefinitely. I would conclude that in a good market condition, every investment decision seem easy and effortless. Most of the investors don't really see through the worst condition and the intrinsic value of the property itself. This is why I want to perfect my second brain to not only remind me the framework at certain times when I got greedy, but also open for some people that really need the help.

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: When is it worth spending more on furnishing or renovation after purchase?
answers.answer: Depend on target tenant and area segmentation.

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: When is renovation just emotional spending and not investment value-add?
answers.answer: Always choose the highest quality of fitting and fixture and disregarding cost. Only choose based on own preference without study the needs of market.

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: How often should an investor review the property’s rent, value, competition, and holding cost?
answers.answer: Annually when renew tenancy.

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: What market signals should trigger a review of whether to continue holding?
answers.answer: Oversupply issue, economic downturn, inflation and increase in cost of living generally.

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: What project-level changes would make you worried after purchase?
answers.answer: Efficiency and attitude of JMB

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: What area-level changes would make you worried after purchase?
answers.answer: More incoming supply

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: When should EstateLab recommend selling even if the property is not losing money?
answers.answer: When the area reach its saturation point. New project is struggling to sell even at market rate/below median price

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: When should EstateLab recommend holding even if the property is temporarily underperforming?
answers.answer: There is booster/catalyst that will hype the market

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: When should EstateLab recommend refinancing?
answers.answer: There is enough margin of equity build during the years. When owner refinance the property and take higher loan, the rental will still cover the installment.

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: When should EstateLab warn against refinancing?
answers.answer: Weak market demand and the building itself is not well maintained and underperformed against nearest comparables.

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: How should EstateLab judge whether the property is still competitive against newer supply?
answers.answer: Price point still lower, competitive advantage still remain strong and unique.

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: If the property becomes harder to rent, what should EstateLab check first?
answers.answer: Proposed rental against market rate

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: If the property becomes harder to sell, what should EstateLab check first?
answers.answer: Proposed selling price against market rate

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: What holding-period mistake do Malaysian retail investors commonly make?
answers.answer: Did not hold long enough and complain cannot sell in near term/sell with loss.

answers.category: Stage 4 - Holding Power And Asset Management
answers.question: If EstateLab can protect users from one holding-period mistake, what should it be?
answers.answer: Be mindful of the holding period before buying the property. Set an assumption and target year of disposal.

answers.question: How many properties should a normal Malaysian retail investor aim to hold before they become overexposed?
answers.answer: Based on the 2 90% quota allow for Malaysian, I suggest to at least buy 2 properties, one for stay one for invest.

answers.question: What is the biggest danger when an investor tries to scale too fast?
answers.answer: Cash flow stuck.

answers.question: Should EstateLab encourage users to buy one strong property first, or diversify across multiple cheaper properties?
answers.answer: If have some cash reserve, financial profile is good, then buy a strong one first. If want to invest but financially not so capable, then start multiple cheap ones and scale steadily.

answers.question: When should an investor stop buying temporarily even if they still qualify for loans?
answers.answer: Have other commitments or life planning that require some ready capital.

answers.question: What cash reserve should be required after owning the first property before buying the second one?
answers.answer: 6 months salary as emergency fund

answers.question: How much of a user’s net worth is too much to concentrate in property?
answers.answer: No saying as too much, it depend on personal readiness and mindset.

answers.question: Is it dangerous if all properties are in the same state, city, township, or tenant market?
answers.answer: Good and bad. If the investor is familiar with a particular area, it's a right thing to focus on only one area. No point to diversify to other areas if not familiar, thus posing higher risk.

answers.question: How should EstateLab judge whether a user is overconcentrated in high-rise properties?
answers.answer: More than 5 similar type properties

answers.question: How should EstateLab judge whether a user is overconcentrated in landed appreciation plays?
answers.answer: More than 5 similar type properties

answers.question: Should users mix rental cash-flow properties and appreciation properties? If yes, what sequence makes sense?
answers.answer: Rental cash flow first, then use the cash out to qualify for the down payment or withholding negative cash flow of the capital appreciation property (mostly landed)

answers.question: What is your preferred property acquisition sequence for a beginner with limited cash?
answers.answer: Cheap property with healthy rental and high bank value. Take the cash out to proceed with next property while rental cover existing loan installment.

answers.question: When is refinancing or cash-out healthy portfolio management?
answers.answer: Holding the property after 3 years.

answers.question: When does refinancing or cash-out become dangerous?
answers.answer: Overleverage and maximize loan amount on each property

answers.question: Should EstateLab allow users to use cash-out money to buy another property?
answers.answer: Definitely yes, but review user financial profile first.

answers.question: What kind of investor is suitable to recycle capital aggressively?
answers.answer: Seasoned investor

answers.question: What kind of investor should avoid recycling capital?
answers.answer: Retail investor that not familiar with real estate market and capitalism yet.

answers.question: What warning signs show that an investor is expanding based on ego or excitement rather than strategy?
answers.answer: Always FOMO when presented a deal.

answers.question: What portfolio mistake do Malaysian retail investors commonly make after their first successful purchase?
answers.answer: They assume can copy the similar return on next purchase.

answers.question: If EstateLab can protect users from one scaling mistake, what should it be?
answers.answer: Make own decision on every purchase and not listening to external advice.

answers.question: What rule should EstateLab enforce before allowing a user to proceed from “first property” to “next property”?
answers.answer: You decide.

answers.question: Which economic changes have most noticeably affected Malaysian property demand in your experience?
answers.answer: You research on web

answers.question: How do interest-rate increases change buyer and investor behaviour?
answers.answer: They will inject extra fund to fixed deposit or bond, avoiding property investment as financing cost became expensive

answers.question: How do inflation and rising living costs affect rental demand and purchasing power?
answers.answer: Does not affect much. People still need to rent a place to stay. However, rental rate might be reduced to ensure competitiveness.

answers.question: Which employment sectors create the most dependable housing demand in Penang, Kuala Lumpur, and Selangor?
answers.answer: You research on web

answers.question: What signs tell you an area is entering an early growth stage?
answers.answer: Look at sales rate of new project

answers.question: What signs tell you an area is already near its peak?
answers.answer: Look at sales rate of new project

answers.question: How do you distinguish temporary market weakness from long-term area decline?
answers.answer: Review from economic factor.

answers.question: When is the best time to enter a mature area?
answers.answer: Anytime if the price is reasonable

answers.question: When is the best time to enter a new growth corridor?
answers.answer: When the area has nothing. Heavily rely on confidence to the developer to complete the township according to masterplan

answers.question: At which development stage does future supply become a serious concern: announcement, launch, construction, completion, or vacant possession?
answers.answer: vacant possession

answers.question: What signs suggest an announced development may be delayed or never completed?
answers.answer: Delayed public launch. Took long time to collect interest and feedback due to no confidence of product in uncertain market.

answers.question: How do you judge whether new supply is being genuinely absorbed?
answers.answer: Look at sales rate and number of unsold units

answers.question: What developer behaviour suggests that unsold inventory is becoming a problem?
answers.answer: Engage bulk purchase community and group to absorb the units.

answers.question: What early signals tell you rental demand is strengthening?
answers.answer: More enquiries from the agent

answers.question: What early signals tell you rental demand is weakening?
answers.answer: No enquiries from the agent

answers.question: How do you distinguish stable rent from rent temporarily supported by incentives or seasonal demand?
answers.answer: Study the target tenant

answers.question: How quickly does rental weakness normally appear after competing projects reach completion?
answers.answer: First 6 months, depend on how many batch of VP does the developer release. Normally first batch will have the strongest rental demand and return.

answers.question: What behaviour shows that genuine buyers are returning to the market?
answers.answer: Sales gallery is crowded

answers.question: What behaviour shows that buyers are interested but unwilling or unable to transact?
answers.answer: Financing concern

answers.question: How do you judge whether owner-occupiers or investors are currently driving an area?
answers.answer: Study the layout introduced by developer

answers.question: When do developer discounts represent opportunity, and when do they signal weak demand?
answers.answer: Developer will only give discount when unsold inventory is high, also signaling weak demand. Note that no discount will be given if the units are in high demand.

answers.question: When does increasing auction activity become an area or project warning rather than isolated owner distress?
answers.answer: If auction cases only occur in certain investment-oriented buildings (Airbnb), then it's project warning. If different type of property and layout targeting different segment of people is appearing within an area then it's area warning.

answers.question: Which government policies or incentives have meaningfully changed buyer behaviour in your experience?
answers.answer: Exemption on stamp duty, higher approval rate of financing, zero down payment.

answers.question: What signs show that bank financing is becoming tighter?
answers.answer: Low loan approval rate

answers.question: What signs show that financing conditions are improving?
answers.answer: High loan approval rate

answers.question: Under what market conditions should EstateLab encourage investors to buy despite weak sentiment?
answers.answer: During economic crisis, ever property is cheap thus it's the best time to buy anything.

answers.question: Under what market conditions should EstateLab advise users to wait despite attractive prices?
answers.answer: Usually there is no attractive price during market hype. Developer can sell at any price because buyer will absorb the units.

answers.question: What market-timing mistake do Malaysian retail investors commonly make?
answers.answer: Buy at the highest price when every booster/catalyst is realized. There is no space for price growth anymore.

answers.question: If EstateLab can protect users from one market-cycle mistake, what should it be?
answers.answer: Enter when others are afraid

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: Before purchasing, what assumptions do you normally make about rent, appreciation, holding period, and future buyers?
answers.answer: Net ROI 6%, capital appreciation 10% within a year (excluding buying at below median min 20%), holding 7/8 years, future exit to both own stay buyer and investor.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What must happen for you to consider an investment successful?
answers.answer: Capital appreciation 10% within a year of purchase

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: Which assumptions are you usually most confident about?
answers.answer: 6% and above net ROI

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: Which assumptions are most difficult to verify before purchase?
answers.answer: Saleability, considering the current stagnant market condition in Malaysia.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What risks are you naturally inclined to underestimate when you like a property?
answers.answer: Saleability

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What criticism from another person would make you reconsider a deal?
answers.answer: Saleability

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: Have you experienced a situation where a property looked excellent but one overlooked issue changed your opinion?
answers.answer: No. But I did mistakes during first purchase. I overlook the placement of unit due to cheaper entry price. Thus, it's harder to sell when unit is located near unfavorable factor such as refuse room or passenger lift

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What warning signs do excited buyers commonly dismiss?
answers.answer: Build quality and management team

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What minimum evidence do you personally need before committing to a purchase?
answers.answer: Accurate data from reliable source

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: How do you decide when transaction data, agent feedback, personal observation, and intuition disagree?
answers.answer: I always trust data first before my own perception kicks in. Data is always reflecting actual market sentiment.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: When has your site-visit impression proved more useful than the numbers?
answers.answer: Every time. As I mentioned, capturing the vibe during site visit is more important than all cold numbers.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: When has your intuition been wrong despite feeling strongly about a property?
answers.answer: Never.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What discovery should make an investor immediately abandon a deal, even after spending money and time on due diligence?
answers.answer: The transaction is fishy, or property status quo is changing (title)

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: At what point does negotiating a better price no longer compensate for a property’s weaknesses?
answers.answer: Remember, you are buying a property. The main subject is the property itself, not the price. Price is just a medium for transaction to happen.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What would make you withdraw after paying a booking fee?
answers.answer: Found better alternatives.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: How do you distinguish a solvable problem from a reason to walk away?
answers.answer: You decide.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: How soon after purchase should EstateLab begin reviewing whether the original thesis was correct?
answers.answer: Immediately after rented out

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What outcome would indicate that the decision was good even if the property has not appreciated?
answers.answer: There is consistent rental demand.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What outcome would indicate that the decision was poor even if the property made money?
answers.answer: How is the decision bad if property made money?

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: How do you distinguish investment skill from luck?
answers.answer: One is able to justify the action taken and does not rely solely on market to affect the price.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What post-purchase mistake provides the most valuable lesson for the next deal?
answers.answer: If you follow everything in the framework, there will be no post purchase mistake.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What evidence should be strong enough to change one of your long-held property beliefs?
answers.answer: Bad property in good location will still generate healthy rental return, because tenant don't care about the quality as long the price is right.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: How many contrary cases should EstateLab observe before questioning an existing rule?
answers.answer: You decide.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: Which of your current property beliefs are you least certain about?
answers.answer: I believe when it comes to saleability, only good property is able to dispose. Those bad managed ones will have issue to sell even though the rental demand is strong.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: How should EstateLab respond when your experience conflicts with external market evidence?
answers.answer: We will see about that. Usually I will skip the purchase if I am not sure about the outcome.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: What repeated mistake should EstateLab permanently remember and warn you about?
answers.answer: Always refer back to my self created framework.

answers.category: Stage 7 - Decision Journal And Second-Brain Learning
answers.question: If EstateLab can protect you from one decision-learning mistake, what should it be?
answers.answer: Always believe yourself than others, only you know your situation best. If make mistake, then just own the mistake, learn from it and carry on.

answers.question: Where do you usually find the best real estate opportunities: agents, auction pages, developer units, owner direct, banker contacts, referrals, social media, property portals, or others?
answers.answer: Auction pages, agency in-house app, social media, property portals and forums.

answers.question: Which source usually gives the most misleading information?
answers.answer: Social media.

answers.question: What signs tell you an agent is presenting a genuinely good deal?
answers.answer: He only approach you once. Because he know there will be other buyer who is interested if the deal is genuinely good.

answers.question: What signs tell you an agent is only pushing inventory?
answers.answer: Keep follow up with you.

answers.question: What kind of deal usually never appears publicly online?
answers.answer: A good deal always taken before the public knows. Just think about this. If agents got a good deal, they will circulate within agency first, then their close family/friends, then loyal clients and potential prospects, only then flow to public advertisement. You can notice how hard for a public person like me to get a good deal when it needs to pass many barriers before reaching us.

answers.question: When a deal is already heavily advertised, does that make it less attractive to you?
answers.answer: Yes. Good deal don't need advertisement.

answers.question: How fast must an investor act when a genuinely good deal appears?
answers.answer: Within the same day, even hours.

answers.question: What should Apex check before trusting a “below market value” claim?
answers.answer: Just check the area median price and the specific development transacted price.

answers.question: What sourcing mistake do beginners commonly make?
answers.answer: They only trust single source, or listen from inexperienced people commenting on the market when those people don't even own a property.

answers.question: If Apex can protect users from one deal-sourcing mistake, what should it be?
answers.answer: Remember to filter who you want to take advice from.

answers.question: What seller motivation creates the best buying opportunity?
answers.answer: Urgency of needing capital/cash due to personal issues (debt, family) or market downturn.

answers.question: How do you detect whether a seller is truly motivated?
answers.answer: They open to negotiation, and will consider your request no matter how ridiculous it is.

answers.question: What seller behaviour suggests they are not serious?
answers.answer: Late on replies, not sincere, keep thinking their property has the highest value.

answers.question: What negotiation style works best in Malaysian subsale property?
answers.answer: Depend on seller behavior. No general answer for this.

answers.question: When should a buyer negotiate aggressively?
answers.answer: When the property itself is not so great.

answers.question: When should a buyer avoid pushing too hard?
answers.answer: When the property has high demand. You can't get anything if the seller don't intend to sell.

answers.question: What kind of low offer is reasonable?
answers.answer: Below 20%.

answers.question: What kind of low offer is unrealistic or insulting?
answers.answer: More than 20%

answers.question: What information should Apex collect before advising an offer price?
answers.answer: Check the demand of the property, be it rental or sale demand. Also, try to look for the rate of discussion of the property in social media if possible.

answers.question: How do you decide your maximum offer price?
answers.answer: At least the rental must breakeven with my installments.

answers.question: What negotiation mistake do beginners commonly make?
answers.answer: They don't negotiate, or they keep pushing hard without realizing the true value of the property for the sake of cheapskate.

answers.question: If Apex can protect users from one negotiation mistake, what should it be?
answers.answer: Advise a max and min offer for the user.

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: What makes a property agent genuinely valuable?
answers.answer: The agent can get access to first hand good deals and quality tenant profiles

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: What makes a banker genuinely useful?
answers.answer: Can advise which bank loan to get for easier approval based on different client financial profile

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: What makes a lawyer reliable?
answers.answer: Can advise based on situation and not overcharge

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: What agent behaviour is an immediate red flag?
answers.answer: Only know how to hard sell

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: What banker behaviour is an immediate red flag?
answers.answer: Only say profile not strong without providing solution

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: What lawyer behaviour is an immediate red flag?
answers.answer: Late reply and no report on progress

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: How do you know whether an agent actually understands the project?
answers.answer: Ask them questions beyond the project they sell (etc overall market sentiment)

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: How do you know whether a banker is giving proper financing advice or just chasing approval?
answers.answer: The banker will make comparison between different loan rates and product specs

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: How do you know whether a lawyer is handling the transaction properly?
answers.answer: Hard to know. Will judge based on time taken for completion

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: What transaction issue usually happens because of poor coordination between agent, banker, lawyer, buyer, and seller?
answers.answer: Delay in loan disbursement

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: Should Apex recommend users to build their own trusted professional network?
answers.answer: Yes if possible

answers.section: C. Agent, Banker And Lawyer Filtering
answers.question: What professional advice should Apex always challenge?
answers.answer: Ask something that are relevant but not directly related to the specific case the agent/banker/lawyer is handling

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: When you enter a development, what are the first things you observe?
answers.answer: Design of grand lobby. Must have feeling of coming home

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What makes you feel the development has a good own-stay vibe?
answers.answer: There are families within the facility compound. Also there are mixture of large and small layouts

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What makes you uncomfortable even when the numbers look good?
answers.answer: The resident profile. Behavior and attitude of people who stay in a development are very important that determine my purchase decision

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What do you observe at the guardhouse?
answers.answer: Attitude and Service

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What do you observe at the lobby?
answers.answer: It's not merely a waiting area. For me it's a welcoming statement. The design of lobby must be comfortable and peaceful to let people relax and chill

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What do you observe at the lift area?
answers.answer: Speed of lift reaching each floor

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What do you observe at the car park?
answers.answer: Brightness and existence of speed ramp/height and width of parking space

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What do you observe at the corridor?
answers.answer: Width and measures to block rain splash

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What do you observe near the refuse room?
answers.answer: Full height/partial wall tiles and ventilation

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What do you observe at the facilities?
answers.answer: Cleanliness and maintenance condition

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What resident behaviour gives you confidence?
answers.answer: Respectful and responsible

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What resident behaviour worries you?
answers.answer: Arrogant and not considerate

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What signs show the building is aging well?
answers.answer: Condition is old but clean

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: What signs show the building is aging badly?
answers.answer: Reverse of above answer

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: Should Apex make site visit compulsory before giving a strong recommendation?
answers.answer: It's a must. But sometimes user ask about new project so no choice. Also you can't make site visit as a virtual assistant

answers.section: D. Site Visit And Physical Inspection
answers.question: If the user cannot visit physically, what evidence should they collect instead?
answers.answer: They must visit physically. No matter how comprehensive your research is, the vibe and feeling you get on site matters the most. There are things that data can't show you. Trust your instinct

answers.question: What questions should a buyer ask the management office before buying?
answers.answer: The outstanding fees that previous owner has accumulated. Also try to identify the speed of response given by management team to test their efficiency.

answers.question: What management office attitude gives you confidence?
answers.answer: Fast reply, provide solution to issue

answers.question: What management office attitude is a warning sign?
answers.answer: No reply

answers.question: What maintenance issues are normal and acceptable?
answers.answer: You decide

answers.question: What maintenance issues are signs of long-term decay?
answers.answer: You decide

answers.question: How do you assess whether maintenance fee collection is healthy?
answers.answer: Based on the outstanding list

answers.question: How do you detect whether residents are problematic?
answers.answer: Always complain on small matters without think twice.

answers.question: How important is AGM or JMB culture?
answers.answer: Very important

answers.question: What kind of management dispute should make Apex reject the property?
answers.answer: Management team consists of a group of self interest-oriented people that only want to misuse the maintenance fund instead of provide suggestion to improve the property well being

answers.question: What signs show management is good but underfunded?
answers.answer: They have initiatives and consistently propose to the residents for improvement

answers.question: What signs show management is simply irresponsible?
answers.answer: Giving all sorts of nonsense and propose useless changes

answers.question: If management data is unavailable, how should Apex estimate management quality?
answers.answer: There is limitation. This requires user to assess through site visit to collect actual feedback. The system I created can't do much on this. Unless you can share with me what your ideas on this.

answers.section: F. Resident Demographic And Project Culture
answers.question: What resident profile improves a project’s long-term value?
answers.answer: Mix of university students, white collars and families

answers.section: F. Resident Demographic And Project Culture
answers.question: What resident profile weakens a project’s image?
answers.answer: Low income earners, foreign workers

answers.section: F. Resident Demographic And Project Culture
answers.question: How do you judge whether residents are mostly owners, tenants, students, families, short-stay users, or investors?
answers.answer: Depending heavily on the layout and location

answers.section: F. Resident Demographic And Project Culture
answers.question: When is a tenant-heavy project still acceptable?
answers.answer: There are family-oriented layouts

answers.section: F. Resident Demographic And Project Culture
answers.question: When is a tenant-heavy project a red flag?
answers.answer: The whole building only has small layout cater to certain segment of tenant.

answers.section: F. Resident Demographic And Project Culture
answers.question: How do Airbnb or short-stay units affect project quality?
answers.answer: High traffic causes decay on facilities and higher cost of maintenance. If delay on maintenance, quality will drop significantly.

answers.section: F. Resident Demographic And Project Culture
answers.question: What project culture makes own-stay buyers willing to pay more?
answers.answer: Low dense, family oriented facilities

answers.section: F. Resident Demographic And Project Culture
answers.question: What project culture makes future buyers bargain aggressively?
answers.answer: Investment-oriented projects

answers.question: What renovation style appeals most to Malaysian own-stay buyers?
answers.answer: Own stay buyers normally will have different preferences.

answers.question: What furnishing style appeals most to tenants?
answers.answer: Minimalistic, Muji.

answers.question: Which renovation items truly improve resale value?
answers.answer: Fixtures like kitchen cabinet, full height wardrobe and etc.

answers.question: Which renovation items mainly improve rentability?
answers.answer: Creative fittings and paint. Also depending on tenant request. For example, students will mostly need table and chair in their room.

answers.question: Which renovation items are mostly emotional spending?
answers.answer: Sofa, TV, bed and etc

answers.question: Which parts should never be overspent on?
